News.title: Russell takes last-gasp pole after clashing with Antonelli in Canada sprint
News.content:
Antonelli was told to calm down by race engineer Peter “Bono” Bonnington after his outburst over the radio after the first incident. But when he carried on complaining, he earned a rebuke from his team principal Toto Wolff, who told him to “concentrate on the driving”.

Then, at the end of the race, after Antonelli went off track a third time trying to pass Norris and was looking to vent his spleen again on the cool-down lap, Wolff shut him down a second time. “Kimi, now is not the time to talk about this. We will talk about this later, not on the radio.”

The two Mercedes men had a brief handshake after getting out of their cars, but it promised to be an awkward debrief.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Martin Brundle said it was no surprise to see the two come to blows given they are fighting for the title. Russell is under pressure this weekend because Antonelli has won the last three races to take the championship lead.

“It was always going to happen. Inevitable. Kimi lost his head a little bit but he’ll learn from this,” was Brundle’s verdict.

The fighting at the front was the highlight of an entertaining sprint race in general. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton looked as if he would take fourth spot for most of the race, only to clip the “Wall of Champions” late in the race. Hamilton was then passed by McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, losing position, which allowed Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc to pass him as well.

News.title: Oli McBurnie spies £200m tap-in to fire unlikely lads Hull to Premier League
News.content:
This is a manager and squad that have fostered an admirable team spirit, although they now find themselves in late May staring up at a challenge on a completely different scale to that which came before. At the very least one could say that they have acclimatised to playing without the ball. Jakirovic also looks like a quick learner – epitomised by his record against Middlesbrough this season. Hull were 4-0 down to Boro at home in early December and eventually lost 4-1, but won at the Riverside Stadium at the end of the month.

The Boro manager Kim Hellberg acknowledged that his players had not been “sharp enough” to create the chances their domination of the ball might have warranted. Their year has taken some turns. The manager they sacked one year ago is now in charge of Manchester United on a two-year contract. Michael Carrick’s successor Rob Edwards is back in the Championship with Wolverhampton Wanderers. Boro’s best player, Hayden Hackney, will now assume – for the second time this month – that he has played his last game for the club.

Hackney, 23, the hometown hero, came off the bench in the second half having not played since March 14 with a calf injury. Having watched the play-off semi-final defeat to Southampton he will have thought that was the end. It certainly is now with Premier League clubs circling, and Crystal Palace thought to be the likely destination. There were fine performances from the US international Aidan Morris in midfield and Luke Ayling at centre-back, and both had plenty of the ball. They just found it impossible to create a chance.

Both teams would have required major changes to be competitive in the Premier League and for Hull, back from the brink of League One, it is a giant step up. They can enjoy their day of triumph but the next 38 league games will be the test of their lives.

News.title: How to have a happy dog and other tips from vets, breeders and trainers
News.content:
Perhaps your dog is easily agitated and you’ve never been able to understand why. According to Dr Wedderburn, the answer might be – and don’t laugh – childhood trauma. “Many, many dogs these days are reactive and get anxious in new situations,” he explains. “They get aggressive and fearful, which is often because they’re badly socialised when they’re young.”

“Puppies have a socialisation window in their brain up until four months of age,” Dr Wedderburn says. “Whenever they come across a new experience, their brain will accept it as being part of the normal world. If they don’t meet experiences until they’re older than that, until they’re maybe five or six months of age, then their brain is fearful and anxious instead and they retain that fear and anxiety for the rest of their lives.”

Trainer Cox has plenty of experience dealing with anxious dogs: “The most important thing is to recognise that the dog is overstimulated and remove them from that environment. Some dogs like gentle stroking, others like a quiet, calm voice or soft food or something else to chew. Maybe a snuffle mat that they can do a little bit of sniffy work – that tends to take their arousal levels down.”

Why are vet fees so expensive?

News.title: Leinster humiliated as ruthless Bordeaux retain Champions Cup crown
News.content:
This time there was no Champions Cup final heartbreak for Leinster, just humiliation. In their previous four defeats at the final reckoning, the Irish province could look agonisingly to key moments when the pursuit of a fifth star fell just short.

But this was different. This time there could be no gnashing of teeth, no looking back ruefully at squandered opportunities. This time they came up alarmingly short against a Bordeaux-Bègles side who have, in the eight years since Leinster won the last of their Champions Cup crowns, established themselves as the new European superpower.

The manner in which they retained their title was, quite simply stunning, with all the damage done in a first half that yielded five converted tries, finished by their outstanding captain, Maxime Lucu, Pablo Uberti, Louis Bielle-Biarrey (2) and Yoram Moefana.

They have not lost a Champions Cup game since being beaten by Harlequins in the quarter-finals during the 2023-24 season. The arrival of Tom Willis from Saracens will only strengthen their hand.

News.title: Uganda confirms three more Ebola cases
News.content:
Uganda has confirmed three more Ebola cases as the burgeoning outbreak from neighbouring Congo continues to spread.

Health officials said the new cases brought the total detected in Uganda to five.

Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains the epicentre of the outbreak but the World Health Organization warned there was a high risk of the infection spreading to other east African countries.

A week after the outbreak was first confirmed, DRC authorities reported that the flare-up was already the third largest on record, with 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

Relief efforts are being hampered by insecurity in Ituri and the fact the outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, rather than the Zaire strain, which caused 15 of the DRC’s previous 17 outbreaks. There are no approved vaccines for the variant, which can kill up to half of those it infects.

News.title: How to get a good night’s sleep when it’s hot and light outside
News.content:
There are plenty of reasons to celebrate a heatwave, but a good night’s sleep is probably not one of them.

You toss and turn, flipping the pillow over and over to try to find the cool side, coated in a sticky sheen of sweat. And the extra daylight is a mixed blessing, making it harder to drop off and trickier to stay asleep once we do.

Light evenings tend to reset our body clock that’s located in our brain. Unfortunately, this is exactly the type we need to feel rested in the morning.

“Our sleep cycle is governed by our sense of light and dark, or circadian rhythm,” explains Dr Guy Meadows, the co-founder and clinical director of the Sleep School app.

The longer we see light, the longer our in internal clock tells our body it is daytime and needs to stay alert. When it gets dark, the body clock signals that it’s time to sleep by releasing melatonin. In summer months we secrete less melatonin, which one reason we wake up earlier and find it harder to drop off.

Temperature is another incredibly important facet of falling asleep, explains Dr Meadows. “Our core body temperature plays an important role in the regulation of sleep. At the start of the night, a 1C drop in temperature is needed to help you fall asleep,” he says. “It’s this decrease, coupled with the arrival of darkness, that informs the internal body clock that the night has begun. This triggers the release of the sleeping hormone melatonin, helping you fall asleep.”

Here, Dr Meadows shares his top tips to sleep in the light and heat:

1. Reduce your exposure to light before preparing for bed

Reducing light use before you head to bed is important, Dr Meadows says. So resist the urge to bask in the evening light.

Draw your blinds to dim the light a good couple of hours before you’re ready to turn in, so that your body begins to step up melatonin production. And don’t forget to switch off electronic devices.

You might also want to invest in blackout blinds – John Lewis do a good range – or at least a sleep mask. Look for masks with adjustable straps that will stay in place and deliver a comfortable, full-blackout.

2. Keep your head cool by keeping a cool head

Dr Meadows adds: “Getting frustrated and restless because you’re too warm only makes your body generate more heat, keeping you awake for longer. Keep cool by lying still and accepting the heat.

“Try focusing your attention on the discomfort and describe what you feel objectively and without judgement, such as ‘I feel heat and sweat on my face, neck and back’. Learning to change your relationship with the heat helps defuse its power and lead to better sleep.”

3. Prepare for cooler sleeping during the daytime

It might sound counter-intuitive, but keeping your curtains closed can stop your bedroom getting warm in the first place, making it easier to fall asleep at night. Another thing to do is to avoid a late dinner.

“Eating food close to bedtime elevates your body temperature, making it harder to sleep,” says Dr Meadows. “For the best night’s sleep, leave at least two hours between eating and sleeping – and limit alcohol consumption.”

4. Wear cotton pyjamas or sleep naked

“If you’re wearing natural fibres like cotton, then you’ll feel cooler in the night than if you were naked, because the cotton will wick away sweat from your skin,” says Dr Alanna Hare, an NHS and private sleep consultant at the Royal Brompton Hospital.

“However, anything man-made or synthetic will keep heat next to your skin. And the same goes for bedding. So if I had the choice between cotton and nakedness, I’d choose cotton. But if you’re choosing between man-made fibres and nakedness, go naked.”

5. Create a breeze

“Sleep with the window open or keep a fan on during the night to add an extra breeze in your bedroom,” Dr Meadows advises.

If you want to keep things extra cool, place a frozen bottle of water between yourself and the fan to cool the air as it comes towards you. (Modern air coolers can chill the room by a few degrees using this principle, although they’re not as effective as refrigerating air conditioners.)

6. Make a ‘cold water bottle’

“Simply fill a hot water bottle with cold water and keep it in the fridge or freezer for a few hours before bed – if you’re an extra hot sleeper, you can leave it in a little longer,” suggests Chris Tattersall, a sleep expert at bedding manufacturer Woolroom.

“Then snuggle up with your ice pack under the covers or leave it to cool down the bed before jumping in – it’s one of the best ways to keep cool at night.”

7. Ditch the memory foam

“The synthetic materials used in a memory foam mattress mean that it’s not breathable and doesn’t absorb moisture, leaving your body to overheat and sweat while in bed,” says Tattersall.

“You know that sinking feeling you get when you sleep on a memory foam mattress? For that to happen, it needs body heat to warm it up, which is then reflected back onto you as you sleep.

“Overlaying your memory foam mattress with a wool mattress protector will help regulate around 75 per cent of that heat, helping you stay cooler on those hot summer evenings.”

Sports.title: West Ham RELEGATED from Premier League after 14 years despite final day heroics as nervy Spurs just about cling on
Sports.content:
WEST HAM have been RELEGATED from the Premier League after 14 years in the top flight – as Tottenham narrowly stayed up on the final day of the season.

A disastrous season means that the Hammers will host Championship football at the 62,500-seater London Stadium next term.









The East Londoners won the Conference League in 2023 and contested a Europa League quarter-final barely two years ago.

But they went into the Prem finale needing to beat Leeds at home… and for Everton to win away at Tottenham.

And it proved too much of an ask.

The Hammers did all they could as Taty Castellanos headed in from a corner midway through the second half to break the deadlock.

Jarrod Bowen raced clear with ten minutes left and slotted home for 2-0 before Callum Wilson added a third deep into injury time.



But across town, Joao Palhinha had already given Spurs the lead just before half-time when his rebound just crossed the line.

That left the Hammers needing two big helping hands from Everton.

But neither were forthcoming as Spurs held on for a 1-0 win after 11 added minutes – so Tottenham avoided the drop at West Ham’s painful expense.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Here’s how SunSport reporter Jack Rosser summed up what went wrong at the London Stadium this season…

From Conference League to Championship, West Ham’s chronic mismanagement has turned opportunity into embarrassment.



Ten years after a world-class team in a world-class stadium was promised upon their move to the London Stadium, the Hammers have finally been relegated.

It is somewhat of a miracle they still had a shot at survival on the last day, but the issues stretch back longer than just this season.

Three years ago, the club were celebrating their first major trophy in 43 years.

Since then, West Ham have dispensed of the manager who delivered not only that trophy but three straight years in Europe, David Moyes, and are yet to find a true successor.

Nuno Espirito Santo is their third attempt in two seasons.



That they were relying on Moyes to keep them up for a third time, needing his Everton to beat Tottenham, spoke volumes.

Declan Rice was sold for £105million to Arsenal, which was unavoidable. What could have been avoided was pouring that money down the drain on players such as Edson Alvarez.

West Ham season lowlights The six matches that left West Ham doomed August 16: Sunderland 3 West Ham 0

Newly-promoted Black Cats produce a second-half blitz for an opening day triumph. Mads Hermansen has a debut to forget. September 13: West Ham 0 Tottenham 3

Spurs ease to victory in a match that would go on to be a costly moment in West Ham’s season. Boss Graham Potter lasts just one more game at the helm before being sacked. January 3: Wolves 3 West Ham 0

Molineux side pump former boss Nuno’s men to finally grab their first Prem win of the season. West Ham fail to conjure a single shot on target during a shocking display. January 6: West Ham 1 Nottingham Forest 2

Hammers fall seven points from safety on a night of VAR controversy at London Stadium. A narrowly disallowed goal is compounded by Morgan Gibbs-White’s 88th minute penalty, leaving the East Londoners staring into the abyss. May 10: West Ham 0 Arsenal 1

Leandro Trossard fires Mikel Arteta’s title chasers into a crucial lead on 82 minutes. West Ham think they’ve levelled in stoppage time, only for a lengthy VAR check to break their hearts. May 17: Newcastle 3 West Ham 1

With relegation rivals Tottenham having finally woken up under Roberto De Zerbi, West Ham need to get something as they travel to the North East. A miserable start, bizarre tactical switches and some shockingly poor defending lead to a fatal defeat.

Recruitment is what has ruined this club.

More than £400m has been spent since Rice departed, wasted by a leadership out of touch and out of their time, relying on old boys’ networks rather than smart scouting.

There have been attempts to refresh that side of the club, in predicably calamitous fashion.



Tim Steidten was appointed as technical director in the glow of their Conference League win.

Immediately the German clashed with Moyes and Steidten was not only banned from the training ground by the Scot, but also his successor, Julen Lopetegui.

The power remains with David Sullivan, the target of fan protests all season, and still the club is an erratic mess.

Even at a basic level, things do not work.

Some areas of the stadium ran out of beer. Hammers fans could not even cry into a pint.



Money has been thrown at problems time after time, to little success.

Deals are left late in a bid to cut the cost, but players are constantly and damagingly overpaid for.

So much so that the club’s accounts warned this year of a serious shortage of cash come this summer, whether they stayed up or not.

A more than £100m firesale is needed before the Championship season begins and the club will have to swallow the fact that they will not be getting the prices they want for their players.

It was ironic that, ahead of the Leeds, game Jarrod Bowen featured in an advert for a 50 per cent sale.



There have been brief moments this year when it looked like, against all odds, West Ham would survive.

But Nuno took too long to settle on a starting XI, messing about early on with Andy Irving – another calamitous signing – in midfield, passing up precious points.

Regardless of those decisions by the Portuguese boss, blame for this circus lies solely in the boardroom, at the feet of Sullivan and all who have stood by him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sullivan did not even remain in his seat in the directors’ box until the final whistle, making his escape early before any potential protest from supporters.

Sports.title: Premier League’s final European spots CONFIRMED as Chelsea miss out after disastrous last-day defeat at Sunderland
Sports.content:
EURO VISION Premier League’s final European spots CONFIRMED as Chelsea miss out after disastrous last-day defeat at Sunderland

THE Premier League’s European places have been decided.

After a final day with SIX teams competing for spots across the Champions League, Europa League, and Conference League, EIGHT sides will be preparing for action on the continent next season.





And that could still rise to nine if Crystal Palace win the Conference League in midweek and take the back door into the Europa League.

Sunderland were the day’s big winners, going above Chelsea with a 2-1 win at the Stadium of Light.

Regis le Bris’ promoted men qualified for the Europa League barely 12 months after coming up from the Championship.

They knew they victory would be enough to secure a place in the Conference League at least, but were helped out by Brighton losing to Manchester United on the south coast.

Their players watched on after the full-time whistle as Brentford drew with Liverpool.

Celebrations erupted when their seventh place finish as confirmed.

Xabi Alonso will not be in Europe next season at Stamford Bridge, though, as Chelsea tossed away their chance.

Despite results going their way – Brighton losing at Manchester United – they put in another shambolic performance and lost to Sunderland, who simply wanted it more and showed all the quality of a side heading towards history.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Blues have spent over £1.7billion under owners Clearlake Capital and Todd Boehly only to finish outside of the European places twice in four years.

Their Prem finishes since the 2022 takeover are 12th, sixth, fourth, and tenth.

Liverpool, meanwhile, clung onto fifth and cemented their position in the Champions League again.

They had to avoid an unlikely scenario of defeat at Anfield and Bournemouth beating Forest to edge their way into the top five.



Bournemouth could only draw away at Forest but even a win would have made no difference in their slim hopes of reaching the Champions League as Aston Villa came from behind to beat Manchester City.

The Cherries still had themselves a Europa League place but needed Villa to finish fifth and therefore make sixth into a Champions League one.

Brentford, who looked in control of a Europa League spot heading into May, threw it away somewhat and couldn’t take advantage of other result, meaning they did not get into any of the three competitions.

Brighton fans and players were watching on after a 3-0 defeat to United, and will go into the Conference League.

A point for them would have had them above Sunderland, but that was never looking likely at the Amex.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Shambolic Wesley Fofana hits new low with red card as Cole Palmer responds to World Cup snub
Sports.content:
RED card, check. Disastrous defending, check. Underwhelming performance, check. No fight, check.

This was a best bits of Chelsea’s season all wrapped up into 90 minutes.





The Blues ended their campaign in a fashion all too familiar with those who travelled up to Sunderland in the heat on Sunday.

Granted, Regis le Bris’ men were always going to be more motivated by the prospect of playing Conference League football, Chelsea did not show up like a side that cared about qualifying for the Europa.

In the end, results went their way to get into Europe’s second tier – but they didn’t show up.

Calum McFarlane’s interim spell ended in predictable fashion as Sunderland showed more determination and interest at the Stadium of Light.



Their 2-1 win was more than deserved, with the only surprise that their dominance did not show up on the scoreline.

Here is how SunSport rated the pitiful players on another day to forget.

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 4

Produced a good early save from close range but that was as good as it got.

He flapped at a corner minutes later and was caught out at his near post for the goal with some questionable positioning.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Should have kept the Petr Cech-like protective hat on.

MALO GUSTO – 3

One of many that most fans would happily not see play for the club again.

He didn’t give much reason for that feeling to change. Inverting on the ball and missing off it as well.

Scored a comical own goal to make the scoreline 2-0. Sums up his season.

WESLEY FOFANA – 2

Much of Gusto’s appraisal can be used here. Doesn’t deserve another appearance for Chelsea.



He’s been consistently playing like his head is on a move away from Stamford Bridge and this was no different.

Bullied for an hour before being sent off for a second yellow.

LEVI COLWILL – 6

Had a hard day with the comical defending going on around him.

Certainly his toughest test since returning from injury but still produced a few big blocks and interceptions around the box as Sunderland mounted the pressure.

One last-ditch challenge stopped Brobbey from giving the hosts the lead before they did.



JORREL HATO – 4

One of the few bright spots of 2026 so far but this was far from his best.

Playing next to a wildly out of sorts Cucurella didn’t help.

Dribbled himself into trouble which led to a Sunderland shot from distance and was outjumped by Luke O’Nien for the goal.

MARC CUCURELLA – 3

Had an absolute stinker.

Like Fofana, looked like his head was in Barcelona.



Constantly taken advantage of with balls in-behind and didn’t know where to stand in defence for the goal.

Got a let off from Brobbey before that after a poor pass and was all over the place at the back.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 4

May well be his last game for the club, and who can blame him.

Produced one glimmer of magic with a cross to the back post but Pedro Neto couldn’t make anything of it.

He’s too good for Chelsea.



MOISES CAICEDO – 5

Even one of Chelsea’s regular top performers over the past 18 months has been running through treacle of late.

This was much of the same. Desperately needs someone else to do some midfield defending alongside him but it’s mostly non-existent.

PEDRO NETO – 4

Can take an assists out of the game after passing short for Palmer’s long-range goal but was mostly anonymous.

Might survive the potential summer cull ahead of next season – but only because other attackers have somehow been even worse.

COLE PALMER – 5

Scored a rare open play goal – courtesy of some pretty poor goalkeeping – but didn’t prove much of a point to Thomas Tuchel after missing out on the World Cup squad.



Chelsea will hope he can find some fitness and get back to his best after a summer of rest.

JOAO PEDRO – 5

If Barcelona were watching, they’re unlikely to breaking the bank for a transfer based off this performance.

Luckily, Chelsea know how valuable he is, it just wasn’t his day.

On the few occasions he was involved there was a misplaced pass for a counter-attack and headed wide from the best chance in the first half.

SUBS:

REECE JAMES (On for Hato, 51′) – 5

No injury before the World Cup, which is a boost. Not much more to say.

Sports.title: Man Utd ratings: Dorgu and Mount star on rare starts and almost steal show from Fernandes for dominant Reds
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED secured their biggest win under Michael Carrick in his first game in charge as permanent boss.

Bruno Fernandes scored and broke the Premier League assist record as goals from Patrick Dorgu, Bryan Mbeumo blew a bleak Brighton outfit away.





The Seagulls were surprisingly limp considering a win would have secured Europa League football against a United side who tied up third last week.

Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players in the Sussex sunshine on the final day of the season…

Senne Lammens – 7

Some shaky clearances when under pressure and stumbled to a few of Brighton’s early shots. The Belgian enjoyed a rare eighth clean sheet.

Noussair Mazraoui – 7

Got the nod ahead of Diogo Dalot for minutes. He dealt well with Mats Wieffer and then Yankuba Minteh.



The Morocco international got forward better than he has this season and linked up better with Amad.

Harry Maguire – 7

Maguire got a taste of World Cup conditions in the sweltering heat and looked steady.

He would have been expecting more a fight against former United striker Danny Welbeck, on his 400th Premier League appearance.

Lisandro Martinez – 7

Chasing an optimistic spot on the plane with reigning World Cup champions Argentina, Martinez started strongly but the Seagulls failed to challenge him and Maguire.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Luke Shaw – 7

Who would have thought Shaw of all players would be the only United player to start every game this season.

The 32-year-old has done everything he could to impress Thomas Tuchel, but it wasn’t enough. He did not let that scupper him today though, the 34-capped left-back worked relentlessly.

Mason Mount – 8

As ever, Mount used his work-rate to impress Carrick after replacing Casemiro in the middle.

He was involved in a superb one-two with Amad for United’s second and covered every inch of grass. It was performance that could have impressed Carrick enough to keep him in house over the summer.



Kobbie Mainoo – 7

Only United player to make the England squad. Right place right time booked for bringing down Diego Gomez as the hosts countered before half-time.

Bruno Fernandes – 8

The freshly crowned player of the season is a Premier League record holder. He is a level above.

It took 33 minutes for the United skipper to hit his 21st assist, breaking the all-time record held by Thierry Henry and Kevin de Bruyne.



Fernandes then thumped in United’s third for his ninth goal of the campaign, while covering every blade of grass.

Patrick Dorgu – 8

A goal and an assist from United’s left-winger of the day. Dorgu has definitely come into his own this season after those belters against Arsenal and Newcastle.

Fernandes has the Dane to thank for breaking the assist record as the youngster worked hard to break free and climb up for his header.

He was the heart of a rampant restart as his well-timed run saw VAR give Fernandes’ goal, a strike Dorgu assisted.

Amad – 8

Struggled to break down Brighton’s player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu early on, but had his best game in months down the right wing.



The 24-year-old looked like he was enjoying himself, which has been rare since Afcon. He was sprinting into the box until the end.

Bryan Mbeumo – 7

His two goals in two games will do wonders for his confidence, which looked shot in recent weeks.

He looked similar to he player that started the season with United. Nonetheless, he has finished the season with 12 goals.

Was a handful when he came on.

Leny Yoro (for Mazraoui, 73) – 6

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Noni Madueke proves Thomas Tuchel right after World Cup nod but Gabriel Jesus struggles up top
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA gave his reserve stars a final- day Premier League run-out as Arsenal kicked off their title parade in south London.

Gabriel Jesus and Noni Madueke goals either side of half-time looked to see the Gunners end their league season firing on all cylinders.





The Gunners announced their team alongside the words, “Your Premier League Champions”, but Arteta – doubtless with next week’s Champions League final in mind – named a team with six players who had started less than five league games over the course of the season.

It would be difficult to imagine more than two of the players who started against the Eagles starting against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest next week, and some players made strong cases to that end today.

Jesus opened the scoring just before half-time with a low effort into the near post before Madueke volleyed home a deserved clincher.

It was ultimately a cruise control game for both sides as they prepare for European finals, and it showed. Here’s how SunSport’s Tony Robertson rated the Gunners at Selhurst Park.

Kepa Arrizabalaga – 6

Made a superb save to deny a diving header from Daniel Munoz after he slipped away from Calafiori. Claimed every cross that went into his box well and didn’t put a foot wrong in distribution.

But there was to be no clean sheet as Jean-Philippe Mateta scored right in front of him.

Martin Zubimendi – 7

A surprise call by Arteta to deploy the Spaniard as a right-back. Only two players – David Raya and Declan Rice – have started more league games for Arsenal this season, so it was a curious display that might hint at how far he has fallen down the pecking order in the closing weeks of the campaign?



That being said, if this was a field test for the right-back spot ahead of next week Arteta could do worse on this evidence – with Zubimendi putting in an assured display in support of Madueke down the right wing.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Cristhian Mosquera – 6

Like most of his games this season, Mosquera proved to be a more-than- capable defender when he has to step into the team.

Today was another one of those games and he looked assured throughout.

Piero Hincapie – 6

While left-back remains up for grabs next weekend, based on this display it’s safe to say Arteta won’t be changing his centre-back pairing next week. Showed his physicality well but lacked composure on the ball at times.

Moved to left-back at half-time when Gabriel was introduced.



Riccardo Calafiori – 5

Lost Munoz too easily in the opening 15 minutes and was only spared from conceding by a superb Kepa save.

Otherwise a largely solid but quiet display. Subbed at half-time.

Christian Nørgaard – 6

Making his full Arsenal league debut with his first start of the season, the midfield veteran wasted no time throwing his weight around.

Hooked at half-time.



Myles Lewis-Skelly – 7

Conducted the tempo of the Arsenal performance without being too flashy today.

Always made himself available for the ball and will surely start the Champions League final next week owing to his strong end to the season.

Max Dowman – 6

Made history today as the youngest ever Premier League starter at 16 years and 144 days old.

Warmed into the game after struggling early on and produced a delightful touch around the corner into Martinelli’s path before he played in Jesus for the opener. Subbed for Merino after an hour.



Noni Madueke – 8

Named in the England squad on Friday and returned to the Arsenal starting XI. Should have had an assist when he played an incisive ball to slip Jesus in for a one-on-one, only for the Brazilian to fluff it. Jesus fluffed another superb cross to the far post was headed wide.

Scored with a superb volley moments into the second half from a Kai Havertz header. A display that perfectly encapsulates why he is going to the World Cup.

Gabriel Martinelli – 6

Had a chance to race through on goal but scuffed his shot early on. Played a perfectly weighted pass for Jesus to run on to before he opened the scoring.

Another game where he put in plenty of graft, but whether he has done enough to start over Leandro Trossard next week remains doubtful.

Gabriel Jesus – 6

Starting only his third game of the season and showed signs of rustiness. Was played through inside five minutes for a one-on-one but looked awkward as he hit the post. Was through again after 11 minutes but was thwarted by Dean Henderson.



Missed a third sitter after a delightful cross to the far post by Madueke. Finally broke the deadlock with a near-post shot just before half-time for his third goal of the season, but his wastefulness won’t do him any favours if he hopes to start in the Champions League final.

Subs

Kai Havertz (on for Norgaard, half-time) – 7

Got an assist from a corner moments after coming on. Only denied a goal by a superb block in front of the goalmouth.

Gabriel (on for Calafiori, half-time) – 7

Showed good strength to shield the ball when Evan Guessand tried to chase a long ball into the area.

Mikel Merino (on for Dowman, 61 mins) – 6

A quiet game as he returned from injury for his first league game since January.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Eberechi Eze (on for Jesus, 75 mins) – 6

Got a warm applause from the home fans when he went out to warm up in the first half. Was always a case of when he would come on and not if. Denied a goal in the last second on the line.



Viktor Gyokeres (on for Madueke, 83 mins) – 6

Had one run at the full-back down the right but didn’t really have time to make a mark.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 1 Arsenal 2: Dowman makes history as Jesus and Madueke score to show no signs of title hangover
Sports.content:
CHAMPS SHINE Crystal Palace 1 Arsenal 2: Dowman makes history as Jesus and Madueke score to show no signs of title hangover

ARSENAL fans had been waiting 22 long and painful years for this coronation.

So no matter the result, it was always going to be a party in the away end at Selhurst Park.





Those with tickets knew they were gold dust, and fans on the trains to South London shared stories about being offered thousands of pounds to sell them.

But the chance to see the Gunners finally lift the Premier League after more than two decades of hurt was priceless.



In the end, those in attendance were treated to a victory thanks to goals in either half from Gabriel Jesus and Noni Madueke.

Jean-Phillipe Mateta pulled one back late on for Palace, however this match was never about winning or losing – and instead all the Arsenal fans were just waiting for the moment captain Martin Odegaard lifted the Prem trophy aloft.

READ MORE ARSENAL NEWS BEER WE GO Arsenal fans queue for hours to fit in packed pubs for Spurs relegation quest

And it was the perfect day for it – thanks in part due to the glorious sunshine – but also because Crystal Palace were ready to party, too.

Arsenal’s coronation may have taken centre stage, yet this was also Oliver Glasner’s farewell to Selhurst Park after just over two brilliant years in charge.



Glasner has worked wonders in that time and could sign out in style on Wednesday in Leipzig by leading the Eagles to glory in the final of the Europa Conference League.

Palace fans wanted to give their players a good send-off before that, which only added to the joyous mood.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Those Arsenal supporters lucky enough to be there got to Selhurst Park early and lined the streets to greet the players off the bus.

They dived into the away end shortly after, armed with inflatable trophies and water bottles covered in the Manchester City badge.



The Gunners players warmed up to chants of “champions” and even those not fit to play came out to watch.

Defender Ben White was in a knee brace, but still hobbled around to near the dugout to soak it all in.

Up in the directors’ box, Arsenal owners Josh and Stan Kroenke were both in town and they will hope this is the first trophy lift they see before the month is out.

Arteta’s team selection underlined that he had one eye on the Champions League final with Paris Saint-Germain next Saturday, as he made nine changes from the win over Burnley last time out.

Glasner followed suit, with his own European final to consider, and benched basically half the team that will likely take on Rayo Vallecano.



Adam Wharton was among the substitutes but came on at half time as Glasner tried to give the midfielder a run-out.

It backfired and Wharton limped off 17 minutes later, appearing to roll his ankle after a tackle with Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Arsenal got their own injury scare as Madueke hobbled off holding his hamstring with seven minutes to go.

Wharton trudging off was the one moment the atmosphere dropped at Selhurst Park, where the home fans were also excited to welcome back Eberechi Eze.



He was on the Arsenal bench and itching to get on.

The midfielder was back at his old club for the first time since leaving them last summer to join Arsenal as part of a deal worth £68million.

Eze was given a standing ovation when he finally came on with less than 15 minutes to go.

He is a hero at Selhurst Park after firing the Eagles to FA Cup glory last season – and one has to wonder who writes his scripts.

There cannot be many players that have left a club on such good terms, and then returned 12 months later to lift the Premier League trophy in front of those adoring fans.



By the time Eze came on, a game that was lacking any real life looked dead.

Gabriel Jesus had struck in the 42nd minute, finishing off a slick move that involved Dowman and Gabriel Martinelli.

Madueke had doubled that lead three minutes into the second half, with the goal fittingly coming from a set-piece.

But Palace rallied late on and they will no doubt want to take that into Wednesday night’s final in Leipzig.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mateta headed home from Yeremy Pino’s cross with a minute to go.



And then Pino thought he had bagged a late equaliser, but the offside flag came to Arsenal’s rescue.

Sports.title: Brighton 0 Man Utd 3: Bruno Fernandes makes history with assist record as Michael Carrick’s men sign off season in style
Sports.content:
SURPASSING THIERRY Henry and Kevin de Bruyne is a lucrative bargaining chip that Bruno Fernandes can now cash in.

Fernandes claimed the Premier League assists record for a season with his 21st to cap a career-best season with Manchester United.





It is a worthy, if overblown feat, Overblown by United more than anyone when they presented Fernandes with a framed shirt with the words ‘Portuguese magnifico’ printed on it last week.

Fernandes has lived up to his billing. A new contract may now be in the offing for the Portuguese, whose direct corner was nodded in forcefully by Patrick Dorgu for the opening goal.

Dorgu does not have a chant but even if he did it would have made no difference. “Bruno, Bruno, Bruno” screamed the United fans.

All of the United backroom staff and substitutes were on their feet to applaud Fernandes, whose name was immediately hollered by the travelling support.



Fernandes has long since made a mockery of the club’s willingness to cash in on him after Al Nassr made them an offer they couldn’t refuse. United have had a happier outcome than anybody who crossed Don Corleone in The Godfather.

The importance of assists is overstated, but you cannot overstate the importance of Fernandes at United. His impact this season has been more profound than ever in his six-and-a-half years at the club.

Fernandes added a goal, eventually confirmed by a VAR check, and was mobbed again by teammates who urged him to take his own bow in front of the United fans.

Brighton could have mathematically qualified for the Champions League at kick-off but you would not have known it. Brighton were 2-0 down when they were booed off at half-time.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Michael Carrick did not want his first match in permanent charge to double as a gimme for European-chasing Brighton. The only rookies in the United squad were substitutes Shea Lacey and Tyler Fletcher, both handed debuts this season.

Carrick oversaw a 12th win from 17 games. It would be excessive to say United laid down a marker but they racked up the most handsome final-day win, despite securing third place last week.

Carrick was the first to be serenaded by the United followers, audible approval for the club’s inevitable announcement on Friday. Director of football Jason Wilcox, watching on, can feel vindicated.

Pep Guardiola won’t be coming back next season and United supporters sounded happy to see the back of him.



They enjoyed a long chorus of “F**k off Guardiola, your cheating days are over” while the Catalan was celebrated 200 miles away at the Etihad.

Optimism is so rife again at United that their supporters resurrected the “20 times” chant, seemingly retired on the day Liverpool equalled them on 20 titles a year ago.

United’s penultimate week of the season was Casemiro’s last. He left the country shortly after his final appearance at Old Trafford against Nottingham Forest yet the United supporters sang his name one last time..

This was perhaps United’s best away day and Brighton’s worst at home all season.



Brighton have snuck into the Europa Conference League qualifiers as Chelsea waved the white flag up at Sunderland. A successful season for the Seagulls ended on an unsuccessful note with their heaviest home loss.

Carrick could afford to give Lacey a 30-minute run-out for his first appearance since January. Harry Maguire embarked on a dribble and shaved the crossbar.

Bryan Mbeumo’s tap-in following a slick one-two between Amad and Mount drained Brighton of any lingering belief with a half still remaining. Fernandes’ early second-half strike from Dorgu’s threaded pass reduced the contest to a pre-season kick-about that the weather lent itself to.

Carrick initiated some forward planning by keeping Manuel Ugarte on the bench and recalling Mason Mount, dynamic next to Kobbie Mainoo in midfield. Ugarte has not had a kick since he started in United’s last defeat to Leeds.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A stray ball struck an elderly United fan in the nose during the warm-up. United back-up goalkeeper Tom Heaton clambered over the advertising hoarding before ascending half-a-dozen rows to check on their well-being.

The fan was left with a bloodied nose. It was then Brighton’s turn to be left with one.

Sports.title: Premier League says emotional goodbye to legends with Pep Guardiola, Salah and Stones among teary heroes given send-off
Sports.content:
IT was a day for long goodbyes in the Premier League as several players – and a certain legendary manager – said farewell after long, legendary tenures.

Bernardo Silva’s Manchester City career came to a close after nine years in the 58th minute of their clash with Aston Villa, to finish their season.





Remarkably, the Portuguese star was given a guard of honour by BOTH sets of players as he departed the pitch. John Stones was also extended the same courtesy.

Both players emotionally embraced Pep Guardiola as they walked off the Etihad Stadium’s pitch for the final time, another man who will be leaving the blue-half of Manchester.

It was already a teary day for Silva as he was crying before he even started the game.

The 31-year-old played 460 games for the club and scored 76 goals in the process.



John Stones was also extended the same courtesy when he departed the pitch on 78 minutes with a non-kitted Erling Haaland making sure to embrace his friend.

Quite surprisingly, not many fans had a problem with the unconventional tribute that took place judging by social media.

One fan wrote: ” Respect.”

A second commented: “A proper baller. Well deserved.”



Another wrote: “He deserves a statue next to David Silva’s statue.”

Guardiola, the man who has managed him for his whole tenure in Manchester, was in tears as his reliable magician left the pitch.

In a true end of an era sight, both men hugged each other as the stadium gave standing ovation.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

City reportedly paid Monaco £43.5 million to secure Silva back in 2017 and that fee could rise to around £60m in add-ons.



Well, there must have been add-ons with all that he won! He leaves six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five League Cups and a Champions League.

Of course, some of those honours equated to a treble in 2023.

Sports.title: Premier League LIVE: West Ham RELEGATED, Spurs safe and European places confirmed
Sports.content:
The final day of the Premier League is here

Plenty is at stake on the final day of the Premier League season despite Arsenal already being crowned champions, with Tottenham heading for safety and West Ham going down

West Ham United have been RELEGATED from the Premier League despite a 3-0 win against Leeds United. Nuno Espirito Santo's side needed to beat the Whites and hope Everton would do them a favour at Tottenham.

However, even though West Ham were convincing winners at home to Leeds with Jarrod Bowen among the goalscorers, Tottenham won 1-0 against Everton to seal Premier League survival, sending the Hammers down to the Championship following a 14-year stint in the top flight.

Elsewhere, Liverpool have sealed their place in the Champions League next season after a nervy 1-1 draw against Brentford at Anfield. They end the season in fifth, with Bournemouth sixth and booking a spot in the Europa League after Andoni Iraola's side were held to a 1-1 draw at Nottingham Forest.

Joining them in the Europa League are Sunderland, who have finished seventh after a huge 2-1 win at home to Chelsea, who themselves have ended up in 10th and without European football next season. Brighton are the final Premier League side to have qualified for Europa via the league, with the Seagulls in the Conference League.

Aston Villa went to Manchester City and won 2-1, Manchester United were 3-0 winners at Brighton, Burnley and Wolves played out a 1-1 draw, Arsenal earned a 2-1 victory at Crystal Palace, while Fulham beat Newcastle United 2-0 in the other Premier League matches on Sunday afternoon.

Sports.title: West Ham relegated from Premier League and braced for fire sale as Tottenham secure safety
Sports.content:
West Ham relegated from Premier League and braced for fire sale as Tottenham secure safety

West Ham's 3-0 win against Leeds doesn't matter as Tottenham beat Everton 1-0 to send Nuno Espirito Santo's side down from the Premier League and into the Championship on the final day

View 3 Images Nuno Espirito Santo couldn't avoid the drop with West Ham (Image: Rob Newell/Getty Images)

West Ham have been relegated from the Premier League for the first time in 15 years after losing their battle with Tottenham on the final day of the season. The Hammers have been circling the drain for much of the campaign and their fate was sealed despite a 3-0 win over Leeds.

‌



Trailing by two points, Nuno Espirito Santo's side needed to beat Leeds and for Spurs to lose against Everton, but that never looked like happening. Joao Palhinha's scrappy rebound from a corner sent Spurs in at the break 1-0 up, while West Ham were booed off by their own fans at the London Stadium with the score at 0-0 at half-time.

‌



Taty Castellanos headed in Jarrod Bowen's corner to give them the lead midway through the second half. But Everton were not doing their bit, having failed to have a shot on target after 65 minutes, meaning that Bowen's low finish to make it 2-0 and Callum Wilson's drive in the 94th minute counted for little.

‌



The Hammers came into the final day in poor form, having lost three straight games against Brentford, Arsenal and Newcastle, and with their supporters downbeat and statisticians Opta giving them just a 15 per cent chance of escaping. Other than a diving save from Antonin Kinsky to deny Everton winger Tyrique George in injury time, there was no magic in the air in London on a sweltering summers' day as logic kept the drama at bay.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Premier League final day LIVE: Table as it stands as Tottenham strike first in relegation battle READ MORE :

Alex Scott in tears on BBC as Football Focus coverage paused as she receives special gift READ MORE :

Castellanos failed to get a shot away when clean through on goal early in the second half and blasted another opening high and wide minutes later. But the £26million summer signing came good when he nodded in a corner and star player Bowen showed his quality once more with a high-quality solo goal before Wilson pinged a shot into the bottom corner in injury-time but barely celebrated.

‌



Yet the atmosphere inside the London Stadium told the real story, with no news of an Everton revival coming through. West Ham's third relegation from the Premier League, after 2002-03 and 2010-11, was confirmed when the final whistle blew a few miles to the north west, with the Tottenham game lagging behind after a farcical delay due to the referee's communication equipment.

The Hammers posted a £104.2m loss for the last financial year and their relegation will inevitably mean player sales, with captain Bowen - their top scorer for a fifth consecutive season - and midfielder Mateus Fernandes, who only joined for £42m from Southampton last summer, the most valuable assets who are set to move on.

View 3 Images Joao Palhinha opened the scoring for Spurs (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

‌



It also has implications for London taxpayers, who will see an extra £2.5m diverted from public services to cover increased operating costs at the London Stadium, where the Hammers have the most favourable of rent deals.

Spurs had taken eight points six games under De Zerbi before the final day yet had to overcome a miserable home record. But Everton arrived in north London winless in six games and never really looked like helping David Moyes keep his former club up in a flat performance which screamed last day of the season.

View 3 Images Jarrod Bowen scored but couldn't prevent relegation (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

‌



Ultimately, the decision to make De Zerbi the third manager of the season, after Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor, has been vindicated, giving a sweet end to an otherwise miserable campaign. Spurs have now secured back-to-back 17th-place finishes and will need a major rebuild over the summer to avoid a repeat.

For West Ham, their change from Graham Potter to Nuno in September has not paid off. Now they are braced for a revolution before starting life in the Championship next season.

Sports.title: Premier League's European teams confirmed as Champions League and Europa League spots secured
Sports.content:
Premier League's European teams confirmed as Champions League and Europa League spots secured

The 2025/26 Premier League season is finally at an end and the division now knows which clubs will be represented it in the three respective European competitions

View 3 Images The Premier League could have nine clubs in Europe next season (Image: Getty Images)

The 2025/26 Premier League season is over but a number of teams are already excited for next term, having sealed their spots in Europe on the last day.

‌



Places in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League were all up for grabs of the final day of the campaign. The Premier League could have as many as nine representatives in Europe once this season's competitions come to an end.

‌



But which clubs will be going on a continental cruise next term, while others stay home and watch?

‌



Find out which clubs have qualified Europe for next season and which competition they will be playing in:

Man Utd star Bruno Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Champions League

Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa, Liverpool

‌



Let's get the easy ones out of the way first and foremost. Champions Arsenal have obviously booked their place in Europe's premier competition and will be joined by runners-up Manchester City.

Manchester United will also return to the Champions League following an impressive run of form under Michael Carrick. Aston Villa will also be in next season's competition by virtue of their Europa League success against Freiburg. Villa's fourth-placed finish would also have been enough to see them qualify, with their 2-1 win against Manchester City on the final day rounding off an impressive campaign.

This is where it gets slightly complicated. The Premier League were handed an extra spot due to its UEFA coefficient, with fifth place enough to secure a place.

‌



Liverpool's draw with Brentford on the last day saw the dethroned champions seal the final Champions League spot.

View 3 Images LISBON, PORTUGAL - AUGUST 18: The UEFA Champions League Trophy is seen pitch side prior to the UEFA Champions League Semi Final match between RB Leipzig and Paris Saint-Germain F.C at Estadio do Sport Lisboa e Benfica on August 18, 2020 in Lisbon, Portugal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Europa League

Bournemouth, Sunderland

‌



With the FA Cup having been won by Manchester City, that place drops down to sixth in the league. Bournemouth secure that spot, having been held to a 1-1 draw by Nottingham Forest on the final day.

There was a circumstance that would have seen the Cherries secure a Champions League spot - but only if Aston Villa had finished sixth. As it is, the Cherries are in the Europa League.

Sunderland will join them after snatching seventh with a win against Chelsea at the Stadium of Light on the last day. Trai Hume had given the Black Cats a first-half lead, with Malo Gusto then putting through his own net.

‌



Crystal Palace will be added to this list should they beat Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final next week.

View 3 Images Oliver Glasner could land Crystal Palace a Europa League spot if the Eagles win the Conference League (Image: Getty Images)

Conference League

Brighton

‌



With City also lifting the Carabao Cup at Wembley, that saw the final European place drop down to eighth in the Premier League. A number of clubs could have snatched that final spot including Chelsea.

But it was Brighton who will be the Premier League's sole representatives in the competition. They fell to a 3-0 defeat to Manchester United on the last day but results going their way elsewhere sees them return to Europe.

Sports.title: How much every Premier League team has earned this season as final positions confirmed
Sports.content:
How much every Premier League team has earned this season as final positions confirmed

The Premier League season has drawn to a close with the table adopting a new look with Arsenal on top and Wolves' eight-year stay coming to an end as each club pockets prize money based on their position

View 2 Images Arsenal have earned the most Premier League prize money after being crowned champions

Arsenal landed themselves more than £50million by virtue of finishing as the Premier League champions whilst relegated Wolves received less than £3m.

‌



The Gunners have enjoyed a memorable week as they celebrate becoming champions and, from a financial stand point, their season could prove even more successful ahead of the Champions League final in six days time, where they'll face PSG.

‌



Every club playing in the top flight banks more than £100m just for being present, which is largely made up of broadcast revenue. Around £90m of that is made up international and domestic broadcast revenue, which is divided equally between the teams. As well as that each side receives around £7.9m from central commercial revenue streams.

‌



Merit payments are awarded based on finishing position and go from £54m for the champions, down to just £2.7m for the team who finishes bottom.

Man Utd star Bruno Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record READ MORE :

Arsenal have therefore banked the most after ending their 22-year wait for a title. Their champion status was confirmed in midweek and they made light work of Crystal Palace. They've landed £54m with runners-up Manchester City landing £51.3m in what was Pep Guardiola's final game in charge.

Aston Villa ended up in fourth, which was one of the positions that needed to be decided on the final day. They have banked £45.9m - 2.6m more than Liverpool who settled for fifth - 12 months on from being named champions.

‌



Below them the fight for Europe was one of the final day's most intriguing subplots and Bournemouth secured sixth spot and £40.5m as Andoni Iraola left on a high. Sunderland completed their incredible first season back in the top fight and will play in Europe, they have landed £37.8m in prize money from their finishing position. Both will play in the Europa League.

View 2 Images Wolves will take less than £3m in finishing prize money down to the Championship (Image: Brett Patzke - WWFC/Wolves via Getty Images)

At the bottom Tottenham secured survival on the final day after getting the result they needed against Everton. That has only landed them £10.8m by virtue of finishing 17th, but truly it has banked them well over £100m given the riches on offer from being a Premier League team.

‌



Conversely West Ham, who did beat Leeds, will take their £8.1m to the Championship, where their revenue will plummet due to being in the second tier. Parachute payments mean they will land 55% of the Premier League equal-share broadcast revenue, approximately £46m, but that will continue going down if they don't make an immediate return.

Premier League merit prize money based on position

1. Arsenal - £54m

2. Manchester City - £51.3m

‌

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola breaks down in tears as Man City players form guard of honour
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola breaks down in tears as Man City players form guard of honour

Manchester City players formed a guard of honour for the departing Bernardo Silva during their match against Aston Villa on the final day of the Premier League season

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was in tears as Bernardo Silva left the pitch in Manchester City's match against Aston Villa (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola broke down in tears as the Manchester City players formed a guard of honour for Bernardo Silva. The whole team showed appreciation to their captain as he left the pitch for the final time as a City player after being substituted.

‌



Guardiola became emotional as he watched the guard of honour before embracing Silva on his way off at the Etihad Stadium. The Portugal international is leaving City when his contract expires at the end of this season.

‌



John Stones is also doing likewise. His team-mates repeated the same gesture when he went off later in the match.

‌



Guardiola started both departing players in what is his last match as manager. However, the Catalan coach will remain connected to the club as a City Football Group global ambassador.

How much every Premier League team has earned this season as final positions confirmed READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola makes final Man City 115 charges declaration ahead of Etihad exit READ MORE :

Emotions got the better of Silva before the game even began, leading City out for the final time with tears in his eyes. They got off to a dream start, with Antoine Semenyo opening the scoring midway through the first half.

City minutes before saw a penalty they were awarded overturned by the VAR. Aston Villa responded after half-time, equalising early in the second period thanks to Ollie Watkins.

‌



Just before the hour mark, Mateo Kovacic replaced Silva, with Rayan Cherki also replacing goalscorer Semenyo at the same time. However, that moment was all about the Portuguese, who waved goodbye to the City fans.

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was visibly emotional on the Manchester City touchline (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Villa showed no sentimentality once action resumed, though, taking the lead mere minutes after Silva's send-off, with Watkins again on target. Stones received the same gesture later on as Guardiola used his final substitution to take off the departing defender.

City thought they equalised in added time through Phil Foden, but a VAR review ruled out that strike. Guardiola ultimately signed off with a defeat.

Guardiola became visibly emotional again after the full-time whistle. He showed appreciation to the fans before striding onto the pitch.

Article continues below

Guardiola embraced several Villa players, including Watkins. He then took a moment for himself to look around at the scenes before speaking with Silva.

Sports.title: Gary Neville fumes 'this is not good enough' as Tottenham vs Everton brought to a halt
Sports.content:
Gary Neville fumes 'this is not good enough' as Tottenham vs Everton brought to a halt

Tottenham's Premier League clash against Everton was delayed at the start of the second half, leading Gary Neville to say 'I'm absolutely furious' on commentary

View 2 Images The second half of Tottenham vs Everton was delayed due to technical issues (Image: (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images))

Gary Neville blasted the officials and launched into a raging rant after the second half of Tottenham's Premier League clash against Everton was delayed due to technical issues. The Sky Sports commentary admitted he was 'absolutely furious' after a problem emerged with fourth official Stuart Burt's communication.

‌



Spurs were supposed to kick-off the second half at the same time as West Ham so the games synced up, as is customary when there's survival to play for on the final day of the Premier League. However, the second half was delayed by more than five minutes as officials worked to try and fix the problem.

‌



Neville was not best pleased with what he was seeing, and said on Sky Sports: "Honestly...what blows my mind is that they have had nearly 20 minutes to check it.

‌



"The fans are booing and rightly so. This is not good enough." The second period at West Ham had already been ongoing for five minutes when action eventually resumed at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Home supporters made their feelings clear and were heard booing particularly loudly before the problem was eventually resolved. Despite their anger at the delay, they would've no doubt been pleased with what they had seen from their team following a very impressive first half in which they dominated.

Premier League final day LIVE: Table as it stands as Tottenham strike first in relegation battle READ MORE :

Alex Scott in tears on BBC as Football Focus coverage paused as she receives special gift READ MORE :

Joao Palhinha eventually put his side in front as he reacted quickest to sweep home his header from a corner that struck the post.

‌



Jubilant scenes followed on the touchline with Palhinha mobbed by the substitutes after Guglielmo Vicario jumped on the back of Roberto De Zerbi.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Those two were involved in a touchline bust-up earlier in the half following a foul by Jake O'Brien on Mathys Tel, which resulted in a yellow card.

‌



De Zerbi was far from pleased on the touchline, and his anger continued over to the two benches with Vicario and Seamus Coleman exchanging words.

The Everton defender even approached the Spurs bench to continue the disagreement after Vicario appeared to suggest he would meet him in the tunnel.

View 2 Images Guglielmo Vicario had a very busy first half

‌



Anger from those of a Spurs persuasion was also on display later in the half when Micky van de Ven was caught late by Merlin Rohl.

Through Sky Sports commentary, it was confirmed that VAR checked the decision but decided that further consequences were not needed.

Joy and relief did ultimately follow moments later, with Palhinha finding the back of the net to put the Lilywhites in a great position to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

Article continues below

A draw was all that was needed for Spurs on the final day, with defeat to Everton and a win for West Ham as the only scenario in which they could have dropped down to the Championship.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Bruno Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record
Sports.content:
Man Utd star Bruno Fernandes breaks Premier League assists record

Bruno Fernandes has broken the record for most Premier League assists in a season after the Manchester United star produced his 21st against Brighton on the final day

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has grabbed a slice of Premier League history

Bruno Fernandes has broken the Premier League record for assists in a season after laying on Manchester United's opener at Brighton.

‌



The Portuguese star had 20 - joint with Kevin De Bruyne and Thierry Henry - going into the clash at the Amex before assisting Patrick Dorgu.

‌



In last weekend's 3-2 win over Nottingham Forest Fernandes equalled the record, leaving him just one game to set himself apart from De Bruyne and Henry. He was on hand to deliver the corner as Dorgu headed home on the south coast.

‌



Fernandes has helped United enjoy a major revival in the second half of the season as Michael Carrick's side rise up to third and secure Champions League football. The ex-Sporting Lisbon star has enjoyed arguably his most influential season, proving to be at his creative best.

Michael Carrick issues message to Man Utd chiefs with talks over transfer advancing READ MORE :

Why are Man Utd wearing a different kit vs Brighton in final Premier League match? READ MORE :

He's topped a host of attacking metrics and they have helped him scoop several individual accolades. Fernandes was named the FWA Footballer of the Year and then backed that up this week by being named the Premier League Player of the Season.

Fernandes is among the favourites to be named the PFA Player of the Year - and that would make him the first United player to win the award in the post Sir Alex Ferguson-era. The Portuguese star, who will be key to his country's World Cup efforts this summer, has claimed that he wants his efforts to end in team titles, not individual prizes.

‌



He recently told Sky Sports: "I haven't achieved everything I wanted. I've never hidden that I want to win the Premier League and the Champions League with the club. I might do it, I might not. But until I get the chance or until I'm here to do that, I'm going to try."

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes' hunt for the assist record has been well publicised

Since Fernandes arrived in the Premier League six years ago no player has created more chances than him. He has created 670 chances since January 2020, 238 more than City icon De Bruyne who is next on the list.

Article continues below

Nobody has provided more assists since Fernandes' Premier League debut (72) and only five players have scored more than his 70 league goals as he continues to come up trumps in the final third.

Sports.title: Spurs secure Premier League survival by beating toothless Everton
Sports.content:
Tottenham secured their Premier League status with a 1-0 final-day win over toothless Everton thanks to Joao Palhinha's first-half goal.

The threat of a first relegation in 49 years loomed on Sunday but Spurs rose to the occasion, seeing off their lacklustre visitors to ensure it is their London rivals West Ham who are instead consigned to the Championship next season.

West Ham beat Leeds but Everton boss David Moyes couldn't do his old side a favour and Spurs stayed up by two points. Everton, with little to play for themselves, didn't even have a shot in the second half until the 93rd minute. They were ideal opponents.

A Spurs crisis averted. There are still many problems for head coach Roberto De Zerbi and the club hierarchy to address this summer after back-to-back 17th-place finishes but they can at least rebuild in the top tier having avoided the financial shock of relegation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Dawson screams in delight at Palhinha's goal

The celebrations when Palhinha forced in his 43rd-minute opener after heading against a post were wild, fuelled by an outpouring of relief. De Zerbi went tearing off down the touchline in delight.

The Spurs fans, who had welcomed their team to the stadium in huge numbers, a year and a day on from the Europa League trophy parade, rejoiced. They had seen just two other Premier League wins in this stadium this season and none in their last 10 trips here. The arrival of full-time was equally emotional.

Palhinha has been a key figure in Spurs' salvage job under De Zerbi. He scored the late goal at Wolves which clinched Spurs' first win under the Italian and he came up with the crucial moment again. But De Zerbi deserves the credit for the way he has shifted the mood. Thomas Frank was the wrong fit. Igor Tudor was a terrible appointment. But the Spurs board got it right at the third time of asking - and just in time.

The big cheers De Zerbi got as he followed his players on a post-match lap of appreciation showed how he is already loved by the followers of this team.

For Everton, it is a seven-game winless finish to a season when they had looked primed to challenge for European football. They were well off their best level they have shown this season, mustering just a couple of off-target headers deep into stoppage time when Spurs' job was already effectively complete before Antonin Kinsky was called into his first save on 99 minutes by Tyrique George.

Everton fans may have just been thankful not to be involved in a final-day relegation scrap themselves, having experienced that pressure in recent seasons. For Spurs the priority now will be ensuring they don't go through this again.

Sports.title: West Ham relegated from Premier League despite win over Leeds
Sports.content:
West Ham have been relegated from the Premier League despite beating Leeds 3-0.

On a final day where only a Hammers win and a Spurs loss to Everton would save them, West Ham did their end of the bargain with goals from Taty Castellanos, Jarrod Bowen and Callum Wilson. But there were no favours from former boss David Moyes with Everton, who lost 1-0 at Spurs.

Image: Jarrod Bowen scored West Ham's second goal against Leeds

The Hammers drop out of the top flight after 14 seasons. They last played in the Sky Bet Championship under Sam Allardyce in 2011/12.

A horror start to the season set the tone under Graham Potter and despite a resurgence under Nuno Espirito Santo, it was not enough for a great escape.

Maybe the Hammers can count themselves a tad unlucky as 32.4 points has been enough for safety on average over the last nine seasons. They finished on 39 points.

It was too little too late in the end as the fans' frustrations boiled over in the second half with songs directed at joint-owner David Sullivan.

The game itself saw Leeds have the better of the early knockings but fail to score, with Lukas Nmecha and Dominic Calvert-Lewin missing excellent chances.

The impressive Matheus Fernandes, who surely will not be playing in the Championship next season. saw a drive beaten away by Karl Darlow but West Ham were booed off at the break after news that Joao Palhinha had put Spurs ahead.

Hope arrived in the 67th minute when Bowen swung in a corner and Castellanos rose highest at the far post to bury a powerful header. Bowen then ended his 13-game goal drought with a typically astute finish from a tight angle before Wilson struck a third in stoppage time.

The Leeds fans were in no mood to be sympathetic, chanting "Lincoln away ole ole" towards the home end at the full-time whistle.

Sports.title: Bournemouth miss out on Champions League after draw at Forest
Sports.content:
Bournemouth missed out on Champions League qualification in Andoni Iraola's final game in charge of the club after being held to a 1-1 draw at Nottingham Forest, with other results not going their way on the last day of the season.

The Cherries were already assured of European football next season for the first time in the club's 127-year history, but they needed both Liverpool and Man City to beat Brentford and Aston Villa at home, with neither side winning.

As a result, Bournemouth ended the campaign sixth in the Premier League by extending their unbeaten league run to 18 games and will now compete in next season's Europa League under new boss Marco Rose after Marcus Tavernier's second-half effort cancelled out Morgan Gibbs-White's well-worked first-half opener.

The home side, meanwhile, ended the campaign in 16th, well clear of relegation, on what was an emotional day for Vitor Pereira's team and their fans following the unveiling of the new John Robertson stand in front of a whole host of club legends in attendance at the City Ground.
